LESSON: POPULATION DISTRIBUTION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People And Population
Topic 2.2: Population Distribution
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Population Distribution, part of People And Population in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How is population spread out in the county? 2. Why is population distribution important in a county?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms related to the economic activities in the county,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Population Distribution in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify the main economic activities carried out in the County,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Population Distribution in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. explain the importance of economic activities carried out in the county,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Population Distribution in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. participate in economic activities in the locality,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Population Distribution in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the economic activities in the county. ●

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Population Distribution in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. sign terms related to the economic activities in the county,

   Population Distribution helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. identify the main economic activities carried out in the County,

   Population Distribution helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. explain the importance of economic activities carried out in the county,

   Population Distribution helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. participate in economic activities in the locality,

   Population Distribution helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. appreciate the economic activities in the county. ●

   Population Distribution helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Population Distribution together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: learners develop the skill of asking questions as they ask challenging questions as they discuss in

groups the importance of traditional culture in the County.

● Learning to learn: learners develop relationships as they brainstorm in pairs to identify aspects of traditional culture in the County

(dressing, food, housing, artefacts, sports, games, festivals, and ceremonies).

Values:
● Responsibility: learners develops self-drive as they share the diagrams of the patterns on population distribution in class

● Integrity: learners develop discipline as they display self-discipline while using a digital map of the County to identify the

patterns of population distribution in the county

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs) :

● Critical thinking and problem solving: learners ask challenging questions as they share the diagrams of the patterns on

population distribution in class

● Effective Communication: learners use appropriate channels of communication as they discuss in groups population

distribution in the County

Links to other Learning Areas:
● English and Kenya Sign Language: learners develop communication skills as they discuss in groups population distribution

in the County

● Creative arts: learners apply drawing skills as they draw a map of the county showing population distribution

Suggested Learning Resources

digital and print devices, digital maps, drawing materials, approved textbooks, KSL Dictionary,
